# 1 Enoch Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**5:1** Observe how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit; therefore consider and know with regard to all His works, and recognize how He who lives forever made them thus.

**5:2** And all His works proceed from year to year forever, and all the tasks they accomplish for Him never change; but as God has ordained, so it is done.

**5:3** And behold how the sea and the rivers likewise accomplish their tasks, and do not change from His commandments.

**5:4** But you — you have not been steadfast, nor have you done the commandments of the Lord; but you have turned away and spoken proud and insolent words with your unclean mouths against His greatness. O hard-hearted ones, you shall find no peace.

**5:5** Therefore you shall curse your own days, and the years of your life shall perish, and the years of your destruction shall be multiplied in eternal cursing, and you shall find no mercy.

**5:6** In those days you shall make your names an eternal curse to all the righteous, and all who curse shall curse by you, and all the sinners and godless shall invoke execration upon themselves by your name.

**5:7** But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, and they shall inherit the earth.

**5:8** And then wisdom shall be bestowed upon the elect, and they shall all live and shall sin no more — neither through ungodliness nor through pride; and those who are wise shall be humble.

**5:9** And they shall transgress no more, neither shall they sin all the days of their life, nor shall they die through the wrath of God; but they shall complete the number of the days of their life. And their lives shall increase in peace, and the years of their joy shall be multiplied in eternal gladness and peace, all the days of their life.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering of the climactic chapter of the nature discourse. The rhetorical pivot at v. 4 ("But you...") is preserved from all three translators. Vv. 1–3 establish creation's faithfulness; vv. 4–6 indict sinners; vv. 7–9 promise the elect wisdom, peace, and long life. The word "execration" (vv. 5–6) is retained from EMET and LOGOS as a technical term for the curse-formula: it is stronger than "curse" and more precise for the covenantal context. Divergences are logged in the disagreement file.*
